answer: Latency-class gating. New identities must pass through a vault of probation: during their first N interactions, they may only submit requests at the tail of a long, randomized delay window, and their arrival jitter is fingerprinted against a shared beacon clock. Traffic that clusters at window edges is rejected. A lone attacker can fake one human's timing but not thousands simultaneously without renting real low-jitter links and sustained idle time per identity, so each sybil costs continuous bandwidth and scheduler overhead, scaling linearly. Isolation scores decay slowly like an ocean tide,
